chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Hakam ibn Hukeym Al-Sayrafi, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I urinate but do not have water available, and something from the urine hits my hand, so I wipe it with the wall or the dust, then my hand sweats, so I wipe my face or part of my body, or it touches my clothes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if urine touches the hand and water is not available to wash it?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of *tayammum* (dry ablution) when water is scarce, establishing that wiping the impurity with dust or a wall renders the hand clean for subsequent use. It specifically addresses the practical concern of whether sweat or residual moisture on the hand re-transfers impurity to the face or clothes, ruling that it does not. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (*taysir*) in ritual purity during travel or necessity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Hakam Bin Hukeym Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I urinate but I do not pour the water, and something from the urine hits my hand, so I wipe it with the wall or the dust, then my hand sweats, so I wipe my face or part of my body, or touch my clothes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from Hakam ibn Hukaym al-Sayrafiy who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I may urinate but do not find water, my hands have come in contact with urine and I wipe it against the wall or soil. Then it perspires and I wipe my face with it or other parts of my body or my clothes. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
